head.h1: How Much Does a Private Chef Cost in Dubai? — What to Know

opening_paragraph: Here is the short answer. The private chef cost in Dubai starts at about AED 700 per person, and most home dinners myCHEF arranges land between AED 700 and 950 a head once you factor in the menu and the size of your group. Two guests sit higher, closer to AED 950–1,300 each, because the full setup serves only two covers. This guide walks through what moves the number so you can budget without guesswork.

replace_in_block.new_heading: Does the private chef cost change across Dubai?
new_paragraphs: The per-person price is broadly consistent across the city, from Downtown and Business Bay to Jumeirah, the Palm, Dubai Marina and Arabian Ranches. What can add a little is access and provisioning for out-of-the-way villas or yachts, but the menu and guest count still drive the figure everywhere. Whether you are hosting in an apartment, a family villa or on the water, the same vetted chefs and the same transparent pricing services apply, with no postcode premium built in. Wherever you are, the starting point holds steady: from AED 700 per person for a home dinner, before you layer on the choices that make the evening yours.

replace_in_block.new_heading: What changes the price the most?
new_paragraphs: Your menu is the biggest lever, ahead of guest count. A three-course Signature dinner from AED 700 per person and a Premium menu from AED 950 differ mainly in the ingredients and the number of courses, while a wine-paired tasting menu from AED 1,400 is a different experience again. Premium proteins such as wagyu, lobster or truffle push a menu up quickly, whereas a well-judged seasonal menu keeps things sensible without feeling modest. Extra courses, canapés on arrival, and a live cooking or dessert station each add to the figure. When people search for private chef menu ideas and inspiration, the honest tip is that the dishes you choose, not the chef's day rate, decide most of the bill. Chef Marco Rossi builds Italian and Mediterranean menus that stay generous on flavour without leaning on the most expensive proteins.
What is the short answer on private chef cost in Dubai?
A private chef in Dubai costs from about AED 700 to 950 per person for most dinners, moving with menu tier and guest count.
How much is a private chef for two people?
For two guests, expect roughly AED 950–1,300 per head, because the full menu, cooking and service are shared across just two covers.
Does the price include ingredients and cleanup?
Yes. The per-person fee covers the bespoke menu, ingredient sourcing, on-site cooking, service and a full kitchen clean-down. Premium alcohol and extra staff are quoted separately.
Does the quote include VAT?
Not by default, so ask. Catering services in the UAE carry 5% VAT, introduced on 1 January 2018 by the Ministry of Finance, so confirm whether a quote is shown before or after tax.
How much does a private chef cost per day?

There is no day rate. MyCHEF prices each meal per person, so a full day is quoted as the individual services you want cooked and sent as one itemised proposal. A permanent household placement is quoted per placement instead.
Is 500 dirhams enough for food in Dubai?

For a restaurant dinner for two or a family delivery order, yes. For a private chef it is short: the entry point is AED 700 per person and the minimum order is AED 900. Buffet formats start from AED 90 per person.
Is a private chef cheaper than a restaurant for a group?
Often, for ten or more. From AED 700 per person at home you get a bespoke menu and private service without booking out a venue, which many hosts find better value.
How far ahead should I book, and how do I get a quote?

Book as early as you can — 48 hours for a standard private-chef dinner, 5 to 7 days for bespoke menus and larger events. Share your date, guest count and venue and myCHEF returns an itemised proposal, usually within one business day.

add_block.new_heading: What does the private chef cost in Dubai include?
new_paragraphs: Almost everything for the evening sits inside the per-head figure. The AED 700–950 per person for a typical dinner buys a bespoke menu built around your tastes, the ingredient sourcing and shopping, all the on-site cooking, plated or family-style service, and a full kitchen clean-down before the chef leaves. The chef also paces each course so the meal flows while you stay at the table. Quoted separately, as a rule, are premium alcohol, specialist rental equipment for large numbers, and any waiting or bar staff beyond the chef. Knowing this split is the most useful piece of planning you can do, because it explains why two quotes with a similar headline number can still total differently. Ask any caterer to itemise, and you can compare genuinely like for like.

add_block.new_heading: How much does a private chef cost by group size?
new_paragraphs: The private chef cost per person falls as your guest list grows, since the setup is shared across more covers. Two guests come in around AED 950–1,300 a head; six guests land near AED 750–1,000; ten or more start from AED 700 per person; and a larger party is more efficient again. Weddings and corporate dinners follow the same curve, which is why a company celebration for thirty reads better per head than an intimate board dinner. This 2026 pricing is a single fee covering the chef, menu, cooking, service and cleanup, with no separate cover charge. If you spot a much lower advertised number, check whether it is drop-off food instead of a chef cooking live in your home, because the two are not the same service.

add_block.new_heading: Do VAT and food-safety rules affect what you pay?
new_paragraphs: They shape the final number, so it is worth understanding both. Catering services in the UAE are subject to the standard 5% VAT, which the UAE Ministry of Finance introduced on 1 January 2018, so typically confirm whether a quote is shown before or after tax before you compare it with another. Food safety is the other quiet cost inside a professional service: under Dubai Municipality rules every food handler must complete basic food-hygiene training and hold a valid health card, renewed on schedule. A chef who works to that standard is priced accordingly, and it is part of why a vetted booking costs more than an unchecked freelancer. That difference is the price of a safe, reliable table.

add_block.new_heading: What extra costs should you plan for?
new_paragraphs: Budget for a few practical extras so nothing catches you out. For groups above roughly twelve, factor in rental of serving equipment, glassware or a mobile bar; for hard-to-reach venues such as a villa on the Palm or a yacht, small travel and provisioning costs can apply. Dietary requirements, whether halal, vegan, gluten-free or allergen-aware cooking, are built into the menu at no premium, but they need flagging early so the shopping list is right. Gluten-free, nut-conscious and other dietary menu options may be available on request, subject to confirmation by the assigned culinary partner. Partner kitchens may handle allergens, and cross-contact cannot be completely excluded unless dedicated controls have been specifically confirmed for the booking. Guests with allergies must provide full details before confirming their event, and myCHEF passes those details to the partner before the booking is confirmed rather than after. A short planning checklist keeps things tidy: confirm your date, final guest count, venue access, kitchen facilities and any dietary needs before you request a quote. Get those details down first, and a rough estimate turns into an accurate, itemised proposal you can rely on. Demand is a factor too; Dubai's population passed four million residents in 2025, and popular dates fill fast.

add_block.new_heading: Is there a day rate, or a full-time option?
new_paragraphs: MyCHEF does not publish a private chef cost per day, and it is worth knowing why before you compare quotes. A booking is priced per person for the meal you are hosting, so one dinner for eight and a day of lunch plus dinner for the same eight are two different numbers built from the same per-head tiers instead of one flat daily figure. If you want a chef across a whole day — a villa weekend, a yacht charter, family staying over — each service is quoted separately and arrives as a single itemised proposal, which is usually cheaper than a day rate would be, because you only pay for the meals you want cooked. A standing arrangement is a different product: a full time private chef in Dubai is quoted per placement instead of per head, and weekly meal prep starts from AED 1,900 a week. Both are set out on our full-time chef and weekly meal prep pages.

add_block.new_heading: Is 500 dirhams enough for food in Dubai?
new_paragraphs: It depends completely on what you are buying, and it is a fair thing to work out before you enquire. A 500-dirham budget covers dinner for two in a mid-range Dubai restaurant, or a generous delivery order for a family at home. It does not reach a chef cooking live in your kitchen, where the entry point is AED 700 per person and the minimum order is AED 900. If your budget is a few hundred dirhams a head instead of several hundred per person, the honest answer is that a catering format suits you better than a private chef: working and office lunch buffets start from AED 90 per person, standard event buffets from AED 120, and premium buffet, BBQ or live-station menus from AED 150, with a minimum of 10 guests and 20 for a buffet. That is a reasonable budget for a chef-designed menu when what you need is the food, not a chef at the stove all evening. Say what your number is when you enquire and myCHEF will tell you which format it buys, and will not quote you upward.

add_block.new_heading: Are set packages cheaper than a bespoke quote?
new_paragraphs: Often they are easier to budget, which many hosts value more than a rock-bottom figure. MyCHEF package menus run at AED 1,200, 2,400, 3,600, 4,500 and 5,500 for defined group sizes, alongside a tasting menu from AED 1,400 per person, so you know the number before you commit instead of waiting on an open estimate. A package suits a birthday, an anniversary or a corporate dinner where the brief is clear and the guest count is settled. A bespoke build makes more sense when the menu is unusual, the dietary mix is complex, or you want a specific chef and cuisine. Either way the best value comes from matching the format to the occasion. For the full per-person tiers and every package side by side, see our prices page.

add_block.new_heading: How do you hire a private chef, and what does vetting cover?
new_paragraphs: To hire a private chef you share three things, your date, your guest count and the kind of menu you want, and myCHEF returns an itemised quote, usually within one business day. From there you confirm the menu, a chef is matched to your event, and they arrive with ingredients prepped, cook in your kitchen and clean down afterwards. There is no need to search "private chef near me" and vet strangers yourself, because myCHEF matches you instead of leaving you to judge. Our chef vetting standard is being implemented across the partner network and covers identity, licensing and references before a chef is assigned, and myCHEF verifies the relevant documentation during onboarding and as part of its continuing partner review. For a cost-focused dinner the default match is Ahmed Al-Rashid, whose fine-dining menus make a careful budget look effortless; for Arabic, halal or Ramadan tables we match Layla Hassan, and for celebration desserts, Matteo Moretti.

add_block.new_heading: How the cost compares with eating out
new_paragraphs: The honest comparison is not chef against takeaway, it is chef against a restaurant table for the same group. Dubai's restaurant market is unusually deep — Dubai Restaurant Week alone grew from about 30 venues to more than 125 in 2026, across 25 -plus cuisines with over 30 Michelin-recognised participants, per the Dubai Chronicle — so there is no shortage of places to spend the same money.

What shifts the value calculation is everything around the food: no booking for a group of twelve, no fixed sitting, no travel or parking, no splitting the table, and a menu built for your guests instead of chosen from one. Set against a comparable restaurant bill for the same headcount, a private chef is frequently closer than people expect, particularly once drinks and travel are counted.
